record.question: You must study regularly to do well in exams.
options: If you studied regularly, you will do well in exams.
If you have studied regularly, you would have scored well.
If you had studied regularly, you will score well.
If you study regularly, you will score well in exams.
record.explanation: The base sentence 'You must study regularly...' is a present-tense obligation that becomes a first conditional. Option 4, 'If you study regularly, you will score well in exams', keeps the present simple in the if-clause and the future in the main clause, matching the meaning.
